findings.finding: Conversation/account revocation during an admitted upload marks uploading row revoked before blob exists. put then creates the encrypted blob, ignores zero-row activation UPDATE and returns success. Blob survives explicit deletion while excluded from quota and inaccessible by normal metadata.
findings.reproduction: Independent test calls revoke_conversation inside deterministic validation callback after reservation and before seal/rename. Success returned; DB status revoked; quota 0; blob exists. Synthetic cipher only for lifecycle; real DPAPI independently replayed.
findings.minimum_correction: Coordinate finalization/revocation with state/CAS and host authorization recheck. Require one uploading row to become active; otherwise fail visibly and remove temp/final blob. Revocation must prevent later publication of any in-flight blob and retain revoked tombstone. Add both conversation and account deletion interleavings.

findings.finding: Uploading reservations have no lease/process recovery. Abrupt process exit bypasses exception cleanup. Four stale rows exhaust the global max_active_uploads forever; a fresh store refuses a different user.
findings.reproduction: Four real isolated child processes exit via os._exit(21) from first stream.read after committed reservation. Fresh store observes four uploading rows and rejects a new user for concurrency. No models/network involved.
findings.minimum_correction: Add durable upload intent/lease ownership and safe startup/recovery of abandoned uploading entries/temp/final blobs. Do not reap live uploads or active attachments by age; preserve explicit permanent retention. Verify other-user admission after real process interruption and byte/quota consistency.
